summary: npm package distributes browser viewport-hijacking iframe payload via jsDelivr
details: px8my@1.0.37 ships a single browser-side JavaScript file (px.js) whose only effect, when loaded in a web page (typically pulled via cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js), is to inject a full-viewport (100vw x 100vh, z-index 2147483647) iframe pointing at https://mfmz.zoeuby.cn/H.html, covering the host page with attacker-controlled content. The tarball also ships update_px8my.sh, a maintainer helper that rotates the redirect hostname in px.js, bumps the patch version, runs `npm publish`, and purges the jsDelivr cache for /npm/px8my/px.js — indicating the npm+jsDelivr channel is being used as a mutable browser-redirect delivery mechanism. The package declares no lifecycle scripts, contains no Node-side code, and would error under `require()`; installing or importing it in a build system does not execute code against the installer. The harm surface is end-users of any website that hotlinks this file via jsDelivr, not npm installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
